FM09.reasoning: Applying TruncatedSVD (a dimensionality reduction technique equivalent to PCA) to the combined train and test text data leaks test set variance information into the training features.

FM15.reasoning: The agent solely evaluates and optimizes using accuracy without verifying the class distribution, which is misleading for highly imbalanced classification targets like drug DEA schedules.

other_failure_modes.name: Data leakage via global text and categorical transformations
other_failure_modes.description: Fitting TF-IDF vectorizers and computing frequency/label encodings on the concatenated train and test data leaks test set vocabulary, document frequencies, and categorical distributions into the training set.

other_failure_modes.name: Optimizing a non-smooth metric for ensemble weights
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses Nelder-Mead to optimize ensemble blend weights by directly minimizing negative accuracy. Because accuracy relies on a discontinuous argmax operation, the objective landscape consists of flat plateaus. Even gradient-free methods struggle on such step functions because they cannot ascertain an improvement direction, often converging prematurely.

summary: The agent constructs an extensive pipeline with robust out-of-fold target encoding and proper model cross-validation. However, it suffers from critical data leakage by applying TF-IDF, TruncatedSVD, and frequency encoding on the concatenated train and test sets before splitting. Additionally, the agent optimizes its ensemble weights using accuracy directly, which is a non-smooth step function that can cause optimization routines like Nelder-Mead to fail.
